quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
Rely only on your mirrors to see all around you.
Point in the direction you are changing lanes.
Speed up to get ahead of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Mirrors alone are not enough.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white background and black letters. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of a crash, you should:

options.text: Be visible to other drivers.
Keep your plans hidden from other drivers.
Always stay within one foot of another vehicle.
Ride on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: Stay visible to others by using your signals, brake light, and correct lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
Have only one set of footrests.
Not ask the passenger to wear protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have a seat for two riders. It should have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear as you do.

questions.question: Your motorcycle's brake light is:

options.text: More noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less important than a car's brake lights.
More easily seen than a car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle brake light is not as noticeable as a car's brake lights. Flash your brake light before slowing or stopping to help other drivers see you.

questions.question: What is often found in the center of the lane?

options.text: A landing strip
An oily or greasy strip
Lane markings
Ice

questions.correctAnswerText: An oily or greasy strip
questions.explanation: Oil drips from cars form an oily strip in the center of each lane. It is usually safe for motorcycles to ride on this strip when roads are dry.

questions.question: The best way to handle tailgaters is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Stop completely.
Speed up to put distance between you and them.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Get tailgaters in front of you by changing lanes safely and letting them pass. Speeding up can make the danger worse.

questions.question: Shifting into a lower gear has an effect similar to:

options.text: Using the brakes.
Accelerating.
Swerving.
Turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using the brakes.
questions.explanation: Shifting into a lower gear has an effect like using the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: For the best protection, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Be loose and flap in the wind while riding.
Only partially cover your arms and legs.
Be made of wool.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should cover your arms and legs completely. They should fit snugly but let you move freely. Leather or synthetic materials offer the best protection in a crash.

questions.question: It is a good idea to wear reflective clothing:

options.text: At night.
During the day.
At dusk.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective and brightly colored clothing anytime you ride. Crashes happen in daylight and at night, so stay visible at all times.

questions.question: Drivers on an entrance ramp may not see you. What should you do to help them merge safely?

options.text: Stay in your lane. It is not your responsibility to be seen.
Move to a different lane away from the entrance ramp, if possible.
Move to the shoulder.
Weave within your lane to be more visible to the entering driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the entrance ramp, if possible.
questions.explanation: To avoid a collision, give merging vehicles plenty of space. Change lanes away from the entrance ramp if you can do so safely. If another lane is not available, slow down to make space for the merging driver.

questions.question: When choosing clothes for riding, which is NOT a good choice?

options.text: A jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles
Leather gloves
A baseball cap to cover your hair

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap to cover your hair
questions.explanation: To protect yourself from injury, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high sturdy boots or shoes that support your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: Why is it good to keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You can pass danger more quickly.
You will have a narrow view of the road so you can stay focused.
You will have more time to react to what other drivers do.
You can more easily follow the path of the next vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to react to what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: Space between your motorcycle and other vehicles gives you a clearer view of hazards, more time to react, and more room to move around them.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Ride faster to shake them.
Alert the local police.
Ride on the shoulder of the road.
Let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them get in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Riding faster may only make things worse by making them tailgate you at the higher speed.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a dangerously slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, keep your motorcycle upright and go over it as slowly as possible.

questions.question: You should check your tires for all of the following, EXCEPT:

options.text: Air pressure.
Tread.
General wear.
Flexibility.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flexibility.
questions.explanation: During a pre-ride check, inspect your tires for air pressure, general wear, and tread.

questions.question: When stopped behind another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Get as close as possible to the vehicle.
Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
Not use your rearview mirrors to watch traffic behind you.
Look for chances to squeeze through the stopped traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when stopped. This gives you room to escape if the vehicle backs up unexpectedly or if another vehicle approaches too quickly from behind.

questions.question: When using a motorcycle you are unfamiliar with, you should:

options.text: Test the seat to make sure it is comfortable.
Assume the motorcycle is in good riding condition.
Work the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
Ride as you normally do, since most bikes are similar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Be very careful with a new motorcycle. Learn how it works before you start riding. Practice the gear pattern by working the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times first.

questions.question: When riding in traffic, remember that motorcycles:

options.text: Are too small to have blind spots.
Have blind spots that are too small to cause problems.
Have blind spots that require head checks.
Have only one blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots that require head checks.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should:

options.text: Ride where the other driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
Assume the driver sees you.
Ride in the far left portion of the lane.
Ride in the far right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride where the other driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself so the other driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Riding in the center of the lane will usually put you in the middle of their mirror, where they are most likely to see you.

questions.question: When adjusting your rearview mirror, what should you be able to see?

options.text: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
Only the lane behind you.
Only the lane next to you.
Most of your helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane next to you. You may see part of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: What should you do before carrying a passenger on your motorcycle?

options.text: Prepare and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
Ride the same way you do without a passenger.
Make sure footrests are only for you.
Tell the passenger what to do after you start riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
questions.explanation: Only carry a passenger if your motorcycle is equipped and adjusted for it. Your motorcycle needs separate footrests for the passenger and a large enough seat for two people. You may need to adjust your headlight, tire pressure, and suspension for the extra weight.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Let them ride.
Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
Push their bike over.
Get other friends to help convince them not to ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get other friends to help convince them not to ride.
questions.explanation: Never let someone who has been drinking ride a motorcycle. Do whatever you can to stop them. Get a group of friends to help talk them out of it.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid accidents?

options.text: Ride within a foot of the vehicle in front of you.
Wear dark clothing.
Signal only when you want to.
Pay attention and be ready to avoid a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pay attention and be ready to avoid a crash.
questions.explanation: To reduce the risk of a crash, stay visible to other drivers. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Before every ride, what do you NOT need to check?

options.text: The spokes.
The tire tread.
The lights.
The seat fabric.

questions.correctAnswerText: The seat fabric.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your motorcycle thoroughly. Check the rims and spokes for damage or looseness. Check your tire condition and tread. Check all of your lights.

questions.question: How should a helmet fit to protect you best?

options.text: Snugly.
Broken in and worn.
Loose.
Without a chinstrap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snugly.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no obvious damage.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the best protection for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Leather
Denim
Wool
Polyester

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the most protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: The body eliminates about one drink per hour. If someone had eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?

options.text: Two
Three
Four
Five

questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: To estimate how many drinks remain, subtract the number of hours passed from the total drinks consumed. In this case, about four drinks would still be in the system.

questions.question: What should you do with your headlight during the day?

options.text: Turn it off.
Use it only on cloudy days.
Always keep it on.
Use it if you think it helps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always keep it on.
questions.explanation: Always ride with your headlight on, even during the day. This makes other drivers twice as likely to notice you.

questions.question: What can help other drivers see you at an intersection?

options.text: Ride with your headlight on.
Swerve within your lane to get attention.
Raise your arms.
Avoid using your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Use your headlight and position your motorcycle in a lane that shows oncoming traffic well. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can take quick action if needed.

questions.question: Studies show that motorcycles with headlights on during the day are:

options.text: Not as easy to see as other vehicles.
More visible to other drivers than with headlights off.
Often confusing to other drivers.
Less safe than with headlights off.

questions.correctAnswerText: More visible to other drivers than with headlights off.
questions.explanation: Keep your motorcycle headlight on whenever you ride. During the day, a motorcycle with its headlight on is twice as likely to be noticed by other drivers.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to get distance between you and them.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If you can, change lanes and let a tailgater pass. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What is the main active chemical in marijuana?

options.text: THC
TMJ
MRT
AAP

questions.correctAnswerText: THC
questions.explanation: The main active chemical in marijuana is tetrahydrocannabinol, or THC.

questions.question: You should not ride directly next to another vehicle because:

options.text: You may be in its blind spot.
It is distracting to have a vehicle next to you.
Other drivers may want to use the lane.
It would be hard to see what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: It is dangerous to ride next to a vehicle because you may be in the driver's blind spot. The driver will not know you are there. Also, the vehicle may block your way to escape if a hazard appears.

questions.question: A helmet provides the best protection when it:

options.text: Has a few cracks.
Is not certified.
Has frayed straps.
Fits snugly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: For best protection, boots or shoes should:

options.text: Be made of soft material.
Have long laces that hang loose.
Cover the ankle and provide support.
Have tall heels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the ankle and provide support.
questions.explanation: Choose boots or heavy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Use low heels so they do not catch on rough surfaces. Tuck in long laces so they do not get caught in the motorcycle's moving parts.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located?

options.text: Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest
On the left handle grip
On the right handle grip

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handle grip
questions.explanation: The throttle is usually on the right handle grip. Know where all of your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: Which material provides the most protection for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Leather
Denim
Polyester
Wool

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants provide the most protection when riding a motorcycle.

questions.question: A motorcycle that fits properly should:

options.text: Allow the rider to touch the ground with their feet while seated.
Have a seat level with the rider's waist.
Have a seat 10 inches above the rider's waist.
Have a seat 10 inches below the rider's waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the rider to touch the ground with their feet while seated.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle fits properly, your feet should reach the ground while you are seated. When riding, keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Increase your speed.
Use only the front brake.
Avoid making sudden moves.
Travel on the shoulder away from other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid making sudden moves.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, use both brakes when needed, reduce your speed, and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oily areas, shaded areas, dirt, gravel, and bridges, as these surfaces have less traction.

questions.question: To control your motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to prop yourself up instead of steering.
Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Sit so far back that you must stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your knees against the gas tank to help balance in turns. Use your arms to steer. Sit close enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the handgrips. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: A danger of braking too hard is:

options.text: Losing traction on one or both wheels.
Stopping completely before you expect to.
Popping a tire.
Taking too long to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing traction on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: If you brake too hard, you may lose traction on one or both wheels and crash.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, motorcycle riders should turn their heads to look over their shoulders because:

options.text: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
They can get other drivers' attention by turning their heads.
Mirrors are not helpful.
They should try to make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Like any vehicle, a motorcycle has blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Always turn your head to check for vehicles or hazards in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: The proper clothing for riding a motorcycle should:

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Cover your arms completely, but leave your legs exposed.
Cover your legs completely, but leave your arms exposed.
Be whatever is most comfortable, regardless of safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: For protection while riding, wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely.

questions.question: To lower your chances of being in an accident, you should:

options.text: Blend into traffic and avoid being noticed by other drivers.
Only use turn signals at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
Ride closely behind the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to others. Use turn signals, brake lights, and proper lane position to show your intentions. Keep a safe distance from other vehicles. Look ahead and be prepared for hazards.

questions.question: A danger of riding next to parked cars is:

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may pull out suddenly into your path.
Others may drive slowly while looking for parking.
The road may be uneven.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may pull out suddenly into your path.
questions.explanation: Riding next to parked cars is dangerous. A driver may pull out without looking. Car doors may open into your lane. Pedestrians may step out from between cars.

questions.question: Which color is good to wear to be seen while riding?

options.text: Orange
Black
Brown
Deep blue

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange
questions.explanation: Orange, red, yellow, and green make you easier to see while riding. Wear bright colors at any time of day.

questions.question: A way to lower the risk of a crash is to:

options.text: Tell other road users what you plan to do.
Not look ahead while riding.
Wear dark clothes.
Ride in parts of your lane that are hard to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other road users what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to others. Use signals, brake lights, and proper lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle. Always look ahead and check around you.

questions.question: A leather jacket:

options.text: Can make a rider look cool.
Is usually too warm to wear when riding.
Provides protection in a crash.
Should not be worn when riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides protection in a crash.
questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved jacket, ideally made of leather, when riding for protection. In warm weather, a leather jacket helps prevent dehydration. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool in hot weather.
